sp:param.name: adaptive-mode
sp:param.sp:values: One of the enumerated values expression, readable, or binary. This parameter selects the mode of the Adaptive output method.

sp:param.name: allow-duplicate-names
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false. This parameter indicates whether a map item serialized as a JSON object using the JSON output method is allowed to contain duplicate member names. If the value false is specified, a serialization error may be raised under certain conditions.

sp:param.name: byte-order-mark
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false. This parameter indicates whether the serialized sequence of octets is to be preceded by a Byte Order Mark (See Section 5.1 of ). The actual octet order used is implementation-dependent. If the encoding defines no Byte Order Mark, or if the Byte Order Mark is prohibited for the specific encoding or implementation environment, then this parameter is ignored.

sp:effect.p: Defines whether a byte order mark is written at the start of the file. If the value yes is specified, a byte order mark is written; if no is specified, no byte order mark is written. The default value depends on the encoding used. If the encoding is UTF-16, the default is yes; for UTF-8 it is , and for all other encodings it is no. The value of the byte order mark indicates whether high order bytes are written before or after low order bytes; the actual byte order used is implementation-dependent, unless it is defined by the selected encoding.

sp:param.name: canonical
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false.

sp:param.name: cdata-section-elements
sp:param.sp:values: A list of expanded QNames, possibly empty.

sp:effect.p: A whitespace-separated list of QNames. The default value is an empty list. After expansion of these names using the for the xsl:output declaration in which they appear, this list of names provides the value of the cdata-section-elements parameter to the serialization method. In the case of an unprefixed name, the default namespace (that is, the namespace declared using xmlns="uri") is used.

note.p: This differs from the rule for most other QNames used in a stylesheet. The reason is that these names refer to elements in the result document, and therefore follow the same convention as the name of a literal result element or the name attribute of xsl:element.

sp:param.name: csv-header
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false. This parameter indicates whether the CSV output method writes a header record derived from the columns entry of a supplied parsed CSV structure.

sp:param.name: csv-quote-character
sp:param.sp:values: A string consisting of exactly one character. This parameter is used by the CSV output method to quote fields whose content requires quoting.

sp:param.name: csv-separator
sp:param.sp:values: A string consisting of exactly one character. This parameter is used by the CSV output method to separate the fields within a record.

sp:param.name: doctype-public
sp:param.sp:values: A string of PubidChar characters. This parameter MAY be absent.

sp:effect.p: The value of doctype-public must conform to the rules for a PubidLiteral (see ). If the attribute is absent or has a zero-length string as its value, then the serialization parameter is not set (is “absent”).

sp:param.name: doctype-system
sp:param.sp:values: A string of Unicode characters that does not include both the characters U+0027 and U+0022. This parameter MAY be absent.

sp:effect.p: If the attribute is absent or has a zero-length string as its value, then the serialization parameter is not set (is “absent”).

sp:param.name: encoding
sp:param.sp:values: A string of Unicode characters in the range U+0021 through U+007E (that is, printable ASCII characters); the value SHOULD be a charset registered with the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority , or begin with the characters x- or X-.

sp:xquery.sp:default: implementation-defined choice between "UTF-8" and "UTF-16". Note that in names of encodings, upper and lower case are equivalent.

sp:effect.p: The default value is , but in the case of the xml and xhtml methods it must be either UTF-8 or UTF-16.
sp:effect.imp-def-feature: The default value of the encoding attribute of the xsl:output element is implementation-defined. Where the encoding is UTF-8, the default for the byte-order-mark attribute is implementation-defined.

sp:param.name: escape-solidus
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false.

sp:param.name: escape-uri-attributes
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false.

sp:param.name: html-version
sp:param.sp:values: A decimal value. This parameter MAY be absent.

sp:effect.p: The set of permitted values, and the default value, are implementation-defined. A serialization error will be raised if the requested version is not supported by the implementation.

note.p: This serialization parameter was new in version 3.0. If it is absent, the html output method uses the value of the version parameter in its place. For XHTML serialization, the html-version parameter indicates the version of XHTML to be used, while the version parameter indicates the version of XML.

sp:param.name: include-content-type
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false.

sp:param.name: indent
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false.

sp:effect.p: The default value is yes in the case of the html and xhtml output methods, no in the case of all other output methods.

sp:param.name: indent-attributes
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false. This parameter indicates, when the indent parameter also has the value true, whether the attributes of an element MAY be output on separate lines. It has no effect unless indent is true.

sp:effect.p: The default value is no. It takes effect only when the indent parameter has the value yes.

sp:values.p: The indent unit is either a sequence of zero or more space characters (U+0020) or a sequence of zero or more tabs (U+0009). For readability, a tab can be expressed using the two-character sequence \t. (In contexts where XML character references are recognized, it can also be expressed as 	). The value of the parameter is thus a string matching the pattern (\t|\\t)*| *, that is, a possibly empty sequence of space characters, or a possibly empty sequence of tab characters, each written either literally or as the two-character escape \t. It defines the string used for a single level of indentation when the indent parameter has the value true. This parameter MAY be absent, in which case the unit of indentation is implementation-defined.

note.p: In XML contexts, for example in a serialization parameter file, use of literal tab characters is best avoided because of the whitespace normalization applied by an XML parser.

sp:effect.p: The default value is . It has an effect only when the indent parameter has the value yes.

note.p: The indentation unit is a sequence of space and or tab characters. For visual clarity, and to avoid problems with attribute value normalization, it is safest to write a tab character either as the two-character sequence \t, or using the XML character reference 	.

sp:param.name: item-separator
sp:param.sp:values: A string of Unicode characters. This parameter MAY be absent.

sp:effect.p: The value of the item-separator attribute provides the value of the item-separator parameter to the serialization method. The value of the serialization parameter can be any string (including a zero-length string), or absent. To set the parameter to absent, the item-separator attribute can either be omitted, or set to the special value item-separator="#absent"; it is not possible to set the value of the serialization parameter to the literal 7-character string "#absent".

note.p: The item-separator attribute has no effect if the sequence being serialized contains only one item, which will always be the case if the of build-tree is yes.

sp:param.name: json-lines
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false.

sp:param.name: json-node-output-method
sp:param.sp:values: An expanded QName with a non-null namespace URI, or with a null namespace URI and a local name equal to one of xml, xhtml, html, or text. If the namespace URI is non-null, the parameter specifies an implementation-defined output method.

sp:effect.p: The default value is xml. The syntax and semantics of the value follow the same rules as the method attribute.

sp:values.p:
A string matching the pattern 
||
|\r\n|\r|\n, used by the serializer to separate lines of output: the line feed U+000A, the carriage return and line feed U+000D U+000A, or the carriage return U+000D. Each of these may be written either literally or using the two-character escapes 
 and . (In contexts where XML character references are recognized, the forms  and 
 are also available). This parameter MAY be absent.

note.p: In XML contexts, for example in a serialization parameter file, use of literal newline and carriage return characters is best avoided because of whitespace normalization applied by an XML parser.

sp:effect.p: The value of the line-ending attribute provides the value of the line-ending parameter to the serialization method. The default value is .

note.p:
The line ending can be any character sequence recognized as a line ending according to the rules of the XML 1.0 specification (see ). For visual clarity, and to avoid problems with attribute value normalization, it is safest to express whitespace characters either using two-character escapes such as \r and \n, or using XML character references such as 
 and .

sp:param.name: media-type
sp:param.sp:values: A string of Unicode characters specifying the media type (MIME content type) ; the charset parameter of the media type MUST NOT be specified explicitly in the value of the media-type parameter. If the destination of the serialized output is annotated with a media type, this parameter MAY be used to provide such an annotation. For example, it MAY be used to set the media type in an HTTP header.

sp:fn-serialize.sp:default: (a media type suitable for the chosen method)

sp:effect.p: The value of the media-type attribute provides the value of the media-type parameter to the serialization method. The default value is text/xml in the case of the xml output method, text/html in the case of the html and xhtml output methods, and text/plain in the case of the text output method. The default for the json output method is application/json; the default for the adaptive output method is .

sp:param.name: method
sp:param.sp:values: An expanded QName with a non-null namespace URI, or with a null namespace URI and a local name that MUST be equal to one of xml, xhtml, html, text, json, csv, or adaptive, in which case, the output method specified MUST be used for serializing. If the namespace URI is non-null, the parameter specifies an implementation-defined output method; its behavior is not specified by this document.

sp:param.name: normalization-form
sp:param.sp:values: One of the enumerated values NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD, fully-normalized, or none, or an implementation-defined value of type NMTOKEN.

sp:effect.p: A value that is an NMTOKEN other than one of those enumerated for the normalization-form attribute specifies an implementation-defined normalization form; the behavior in this case is not specified by this document. The default value is none.

sp:param.name: omit-xml-declaration
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false.

sp:param.name: standalone
sp:param.sp:values: Either a boolean value, true or false, or the value or omit.

sp:effect.p: The default value is omit; this means that no standalone attribute is to be included in the XML declaration.

sp:param.name: suppress-indentation
sp:param.sp:values: A list of expanded QNames, possibly empty.

sp:effect.p:
A whitespace-separated list of QNames. The default value is an empty list. After expansion of these names using the
for the xsl:output declaration in which they appear, this list of names provides the value of the suppress-indentation parameter to the serialization method. In the case of an unprefixed name, the default namespace (that is, the namespace declared using xmlns="uri") is used.

note.p: This differs from the rule for most other QNames used in a stylesheet. The reason is that these names refer to elements in the result document, and therefore follow the same convention as the name of a literal result element or the name attribute of xsl:element.

sp:param.name: undeclare-prefixes
sp:param.sp:values: A boolean value, true or false.

sp:param.name: use-character-maps
sp:param.sp:values: A list of pairs, possibly empty, with each pair consisting of a single Unicode character and a string of Unicode characters.

sp:effect.p: A list of named character maps that are used in conjunction with this output definition. The way this attribute is used is described in . The default value is an empty list.

sp:param.name: version
sp:param.sp:values: A string of Unicode characters. This parameter MAY be absent.

sp:effect.p: The value of the version attribute provides the value of the version parameter to the serialization method. The set of permitted values, and the default value, are implementation-defined. A serialization error will be raised if the requested version is not supported by the implementation.
